author: MARUM – Zentrum für Marine Umweltwissenschaften, Universität Bremen; V. Diekamp
why: A crew member steadies the MARUM-SQUID remotely operated vehicle as it goes over the side of the research ship Meteor in the Atlantic south of the Azores: deep-sea fieldwork in the waters this degree studies from Ponta Delgada and Horta.
cropNote: Landscape 3000x1965; the 16:10 centre keeps the man in a hard hat at left and the whole ROV over open sea, subject in the upper half. The vehicle's name plate ("marum 1705") is about 5 px high at 480 px and not legible; no other text; one three-quarter profile, no crowd.

commonsFile: Déploiement d'une bathysonde depuis le Pourquoi pas? (Ifremer 00735-84681 - 40246).jpg
author: Olivier Dugornay
why: Two crew in red helmets at the hangar door of the research vessel Pourquoi pas? swing a CTD rosette of water-sampling bottles out over the sea: measuring the water column, the ocean data that this degree's science, economics and policy courses start from.
cropNote: Landscape 8256x5504; the 16:10 centre keeps both crew at left and the rosette over blue water at right; a green exit pictogram top-left has no words; the coast behind is soft. A winch-lowered sampler from a ship's hangar, distinct from the Azores ROV card and from NL Leiden's small-boat river sampler.

author: ManuelSchottdorf
why: Rat cortical neurons grown on a coverslip and made to glow with green fluorescent protein: the cells and the connections between them that systems and cognitive neuroscience traces from circuits to behaviour.
cropNote: Fluorescence micrograph 2317x1992; the 16:10 centre is an even field of cell bodies and branching neurites, teal on black, with no scale bar, labels or text. Dark overall but the pattern holds under both veils. Not a brain model (ES UC3M), EEG cap (DE, NL) or MRI scanner (NL UvA).

author: Drnoble
why: Close up on the hinged joints of a Pelamis wave-energy converter: hydraulic rams between the steel tube sections that turn the flexing of the swell into pumped oil and then electricity. Structures, hydraulics and power conversion in one mechanism, the breadth Técnico's General Engineering covers before you choose a pathway; the first Pelamis wave farm was off Aguçadoura in northern Portugal.
cropNote: Landscape 4755x3160; the 16:10 centre is a tight diagonal of red tube sections, two joints with their black ram shafts and a walkway rail, blue water only at the edges; no horizon, no people, no text or logos. A close-up of a mechanism, not a red machine standing in open water (Italy's MOSE card), and replaces the distant Aguçadoura wave-farm frame.

author: USAID Ethiopia from Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
why: A spray operator in coveralls, face shield and mask fills his sprayer before indoor residual spraying against malaria mosquitoes in Oromia, Ethiopia: prevention delivered house by house, the kind of programme global public health plans, runs and evaluates.
cropNote: Landscape 2048x1360; the 16:10 centre keeps the operator, his gloved hands and the bucket against a mud-brick wall; the agency stripe on his hard hat sits at the top edge, blurred and illegible at 480 px (like the tolerated vest marks); one adult, no children, no signage.
